notes: Dispute over priority between a landlord's statutory lien and a chattel mortgage on billiard tables in a month-to-month commercial store-house tenancy; no household lodging/boarding issue.
Adverse possession of a town street fenced by permission of town council; landlord/tenant relation invoked only by analogy to permissive possession, not household letting.
Mortgagor/mortgagee rights to ungathered crops on farm land worked under a farming partnership/tenancy; agricultural rent law, no household lodging issue.
Trespass-to-try-title dispute among tenants in common over land and joint liability of co-defendants for rents/waste; no lodging or boarding issue.
Constitutional/statutory construction of county authority to levy a special tax for building an addition to a courthouse; unrelated to letting or lodging.
Adverse possession/limitation dispute between tenants in common claiming land by heirship; no household letting or boarding issue.

Farm land leased for three years with sub-rental to another tenant; suit concerns whether a judgment against the tenant (in a suit landlord had no notice of) binds the landlord in a later title dispute. Agricultural land lease, not household lodging; characterization ('lease') is from the underlying facts only, not doctrinally at issue, so holding_summary/quotes omitted.
Privity of contract/estate between landlord and sub-tenant on a farm as to landlord's distress-warrant remedy against sub-tenant's crops; agricultural rent law, no household lodging issue.

Slander suit by a boarding-house keeper; the boarding house is mentioned only as a source of special damages (boarders leaving after the slander), not as an occasion for the court to characterize the letting/boarding arrangement or its regulation. Passing mention, not doctrinal engagement.

Commercial lot leaseholder sub-let a lot by the month to a tenant who held over; issue is purely procedural (whether trespass to try title lies in district court for a term-of-years interest vs. forcible-detainer in justice court). No household lodging/boarding issue.

Homestead-exemption case: owner rented out his former place-of-business store-house for mercantile use by others after ceasing his own business there. Concerns the 'place of business' homestead exemption and abandonment, not the legal character or regulation of household lodging/boarding; renting was to a mercantile tenant, not a lodger/boarder.

Deed-absolute-as-mortgage dispute; grantor stayed in possession of his homestead under a lease-like arrangement with the grantee as security device. Mortgage/security-interest doctrine, not household lodging.

Trespass to try title; whether a default judgment against a farm tenant (Caffey), obtained without notice to his landlord, binds the landlord in a later suit over the same land. No household lodging issue.
Validity of an alleged parol gift of land and of a probate-court partition/sale binding minor heirs; unrelated to letting or lodging.
Suit for value of timber cut from land owned by tenants in common, with a set-off dispute; a joinder-of-co-tenants procedural question. Unrelated to lodging/boarding.
Trespass to try title turning on whether a plaintiff pleading sole heirship can recover despite proof of other living heirs; unrelated to letting or lodging.

Commercial lease of gin shops, mill, oxen, wagon and dwelling houses between business partners for a fixed monthly rent; dispute is whether a covenant to redeliver property 'in good running order' obliges the lessee to rebuild after accidental fire. Industrial/commercial lease, not household lodging.

holding_summary: A city ordinance made it a criminal offense to rent, let or lease any premises within the city limits to a prostitute or lewd woman, without regard to the use to which the premises were put; the mayor was removed from office by the city aldermen for renting a house to such a woman. The Texas Supreme Court held the ordinance null and void as an unreasonable, proscriptive denial of shelter to an 'unfortunate class' and in contravention of common right, and accordingly voided the mayor's removal.

quotes.text: any person who shall knowingly furnish, rent, let or lease any premises or place within the city Emits to any prostitute or lewd woman, or to any person for their use, shaU be deemed guilty of an offense.

That unfortunate and degraded class against whom the ordinance was mainly intended, however far they may have fallen beneath the true mission of women, which it is one oh our highest duties to foster and protect in social and domestic life, are still human beings, entitled to shelter and the protection of the law; and the council did not have the power to so far proscribe them as a class, as to make it a penal offense in any one to rent them a habitation without regard to its use.
Such an ordinance is null and void, because unreasonable and in contravention of common right.

notes: Favorable on the level-of-generality point: the court strikes down a municipal attempt to criminalize renting property to a disfavored class of occupant, treating the right to let a habitation as protected regardless of the letter's identity or purpose. The opinion never specifies whether Milliken owned/occupied the house himself or as pure investment property, nor the term of the tenancy, so who_was_letting and duration_of_occupancy are left unclear; characterization left null because the court addresses the ordinance's validity, not whether the arrangement was a lease/license/lodging.
